info.title: AccessFlow API
info.description:
The JSON API of AccessFlow, used by its web UI. **Read-only documentation**: requests cannot be sent from this page.

- **Sessions:** `POST /auth/login` sets the `accessflow_session` cookie (HttpOnly) and the `accessflow_csrf` cookie. Every signed-in `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` must send the `X-CSRF-Token` header with the value of the `accessflow_csrf` cookie. Cross-site unsafe requests, sign-in included, are rejected with `403 cross_origin_request`.
- **Errors** are JSON `{"error": "<code>"}`, plus `field` for a validation error and `expected` when a value differs from a defined one only in case. Every signed-in operation can return `401 authentication_required`; an unknown `/api` path is `404 not_found`, a wrong method `405 method_not_allowed`, an unexpected failure `500 internal_error`.
- **Request bodies** are one JSON value of at most 64 KiB (the workbook upload excepted); a malformed body or an unknown key is `400 invalid_json`.
- **Concurrency:** records that can change carry a `version`; a stale one is `409 version_conflict`.
- **Auditor:** an account holding `AUDITOR` is an external auditor and reaches only `GET /audit/events`, `GET /audit/events/export`, `GET /audit/filters`, `GET /audit/access` and `GET /audit/requests` (plus `/auth`), whatever other roles it holds; every other operation, the evidence reports included, answers `403 forbidden` (DECISIONS.md O7 notes 2026-10-31).
- **Rules:** the business rules behind each endpoint are in `docs/api.md` and `DECISIONS.md`. Every permission is enforced by the server.

Mock email delivery and the demo accounts are for local demonstration only.

post.description: Public; no CSRF token (none exists yet). Checks the password and sets two cookies: `accessflow_session` (HttpOnly, signed token) and `accessflow_csrf` (readable; echo it in `X-CSRF-Token` on unsafe requests). Every failure (unknown email, wrong password, locked, inactive) is one generic `401 invalid_credentials`; 5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes. Rate limited per client address.

post.description: Never yourself. A Super Admin nominates an active employee for a two-person promotion; it expires after 7 days and the authorizers (other Super Admins, else InfoSec) are notified. An HR Manager who is not a Super Admin starts a succession while at most one Super Admin has not left (active or suspended; D2 notes 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31): `succession: true`. No link is sent yet: InfoSec members and Super Admins other than the proposer and nominee are notified, and one of them must authorize it (`POST …/authorize`). Only then does the nominee get a single-use 24-hour role-acceptance link in their own Mock Email Outbox (audited as `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLE_LINK_ISSUED`, without the token).

post.description: Never the nominee or the proposer. A Super Admin other than those two decides when one is active; otherwise, and always for a recovery nomination, an InfoSec member decides.
